I can only see the new version here — the diff didn't come through, just the final `format_username` function. To confirm no logic got flipped I'd need the original nested if/else to compare against. Could you paste the "before" version (or the actual diff with `-`/`+` lines)?

That said, a couple things worth flagging just from reading this version on its own:

1. **Order of checks**: `not name` is checked before `.strip()`. If `name` is a string of only whitespace (e.g. `"   "`), it's truthy, so it skips the "unknown" branch, gets stripped to `""`, and then falls through to `return name` — returning an empty string rather than `"unknown"`. Worth checking whether the original handled that case (stripping before the falsy check) — if so, this would be a behavior change, not just a refactor.
2. **Boundary case**: `len(name) > 20` truncates to `name[:20] + "..."`. Confirm the original used `> 20` (not `>= 20` or a different length) and truncated to the same slice length — off-by-one errors are common in this kind of refactor.

Send over the original and I'll do a line-by-line comparison.
